simplified_text: Develop Hindi by drawing from Sanskrit and other Indian languages

title: Proclamation of Emergency
original_text: If the President is satisfied that a grave emergency exists whereby the security of India or of any part of the territory thereof is threatened, whether by war or external aggression or armed rebellion, he may, by Proclamation, make a declaration to that effect. A Proclamation of Emergency must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month.
simplified_text: President can proclaim Emergency due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion

title: Effect of Proclamation of Emergency
original_text: While a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, the executive power of the Union shall extend to giving directions to any State as to the manner in which the executive power thereof is to be exercised. Parliament shall have power to make laws for the whole or any part of the territory of India with respect to any matter in the State List.
simplified_text: During Emergency, Union's executive power extends to directing States

title: Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in States
original_text: If the President, on receipt of a report from the Governor of a State or otherwise, is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution, the President may by Proclamation assume to himself all or any of the functions of the Government of the State and declare that the powers of the Legislature of the State shall be exercisable by or under the authority of Parliament.
simplified_text: President's Rule - President can assume State functions

title: Exercise of legislative powers under Proclamation issued under article 356
original_text: Where a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation in any State, Parliament shall have power to make laws with respect to any matter in the State List and to confer powers and impose duties on the Union or officers and authorities of the Union.
simplified_text: Parliament can legislate for State during President's Rule

title: Suspension of provisions of article 19 during emergencies
original_text: While a Proclamation of Emergency declaring that the security of India or any part thereof is threatened by war or by external aggression is in operation, nothing in article 19 shall restrict the power of the State to make any law or to take any executive action.
simplified_text: Article 19 (six freedoms) suspended during Emergency

title: Suspension of the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III during emergencies
original_text: Where a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, the President may by order declare that the right to move any court for the enforcement of such of the rights conferred by Part III as may be mentioned in the order and all proceedings pending in any court for the enforcement of the rights so mentioned shall remain suspended for the period during which the Proclamation is in force.
simplified_text: President can suspend right to move court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights

title: Provisions as to financial emergency
original_text: If the President is satisfied that a situation has arisen whereby the financial stability or credit of India or of any part of the territory thereof is threatened, he may by a Proclamation make a declaration to that effect (Financial Emergency). During Financial Emergency, the executive authority of the Union shall extend to the giving of directions to any State to observe such canons of financial propriety as may be specified in the directions.
simplified_text: President can proclaim Financial Emergency

title: Protection of President and Governors
original_text: The President, or the Governor of a State, shall not be answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his office. No criminal proceedings whatsoever shall be instituted or continued against the President, or the Governor of a State, in any court during his term of office.
simplified_text: President and Governors immune from court proceedings

title: Protection of publication of proceedings of Parliament and State Legislatures
original_text: No person shall be liable to any civil or criminal proceedings in any court in respect of the publication in a newspaper of a substantially true report of any proceedings of either House of Parliament or the Legislative Assembly, or either House of the Legislature, of a State, unless the publication is proved to have been made with malice.
simplified_text: No liability for publishing parliamentary proceedings

title: Bar to interference by courts in disputes arising out of certain treaties, agreements, etc.
original_text: Neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall have jurisdiction in any dispute arising out of any provision of a treaty, agreement, covenant, engagement, sanad or other similar instrument which was entered into or executed before the commencement of this Constitution.
simplified_text: Courts cannot interfere in disputes arising from treaties before Constitution

title: Effect of failure to comply with, or to give effect to, directions given by the Union
original_text: Where any State has failed to comply with or to give effect to any directions given in the exercise of the executive power of the Union, it shall be lawful for the President to hold that a situation has arisen in which the Government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution.
simplified_text: President can declare constitutional breakdown if State fails to comply with Union directions

title: Definitions
original_text: In this Constitution, unless the context otherwise requires, various terms are defined including: 'agricultural income', 'appropriate Legislature', 'Constitution', 'corporation tax', 'debt', 'estate duty', 'existing law', 'Federal Court', 'goods', 'guarantee', 'High Court', 'Indian State', 'net proceeds', 'pension', 'Proclamation of Emergency', 'public notification', 'railway', 'Scheduled Castes', 'Scheduled Tribes', 'securities', 'tax on income', 'tax on the sale or purchase of goods', 'taxation laws', 'Union territory'.
simplified_text: Definitions of various terms used in Constitution

title: Interpretation
original_text: Unless the context otherwise requires, the General Clauses Act, 1897, shall apply for the interpretation of this Constitution as it applies for the interpretation of an Act of the Legislature of the Dominion of India.
simplified_text: General interpretation provisions

title: Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor
original_text: Parliament may amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of this Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down in this article. An amendment Bill must be passed in each House by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting. If the amendment seeks to make any change in certain specified provisions (federal structure, Fundamental Rights, etc.), the amendment must also be ratified by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States before the Bill is presented to the President for assent.
simplified_text: Parliament can amend Constitution by special majority

title: Temporary provisions with respect to the State of Jammu and Kashmir (Repealed)
original_text: Article 370, which granted special autonomous status to Jammu and Kashmir, was abrogated by the Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order, 2019 on 5 August 2019. The state was reorganized into two Union Territories: Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.
simplified_text: Special status for J&K - Abrogated on 5 August 2019

title: Special provision with respect to the States of Maharashtra and Gujarat
original_text: The President may provide for equitable allocation of funds for developmental expenditure over the State, having regard to the requirements of the different areas, particularly Vidarbha and Marathwada in Maharashtra, and Saurashtra and Kutch in Gujarat.
simplified_text: Special provisions for development of Vidarbha, Marathwada, Saurashtra, Kutch

title: Special provision with respect to the State of Nagaland
original_text: No Act of Parliament in respect of religious or social practices of the Nagas, Naga customary law and procedure, administration of civil and criminal justice involving decisions according to Naga customary law, and ownership and transfer of land and its resources, shall apply to the State of Nagaland unless the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland by a resolution so decides.
simplified_text: Special provisions for Nagaland regarding customary law

title: Special provision with respect to the State of Assam
original_text: The Legislative Assembly of the State of Assam shall consist of not less than one hundred and eight and not more than one hundred and twenty-six members. There shall be a Committee of the Legislative Assembly consisting of members elected from the tribal areas to deal with matters affecting tribal areas.
simplified_text: Committee for tribal areas in Assam

title: Special provision with respect to the State of Manipur
original_text: There shall be a Committee of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Manipur consisting of members of that Assembly elected from the Hill Areas of that State, to deal with matters relating to the administration of the Hill Areas.
simplified_text: Committee for Hill Areas in Manipur

title: Special provisions with respect to the State of Andhra Pradesh or the State of Telangana
original_text: The President may provide for equitable opportunities and facilities for the people belonging to different parts of the State of Andhra Pradesh or Telangana in the matter of public employment and in the matter of education.
simplified_text: Equitable opportunities for people of different regions in public employment and education

title: Establishment of Central University in Andhra Pradesh
original_text: Parliament may by law provide for the establishment of a University in the State of Andhra Pradesh.
simplified_text: Central University established in Andhra Pradesh

title: Special provisions with respect to the State of Sikkim
original_text: Special provisions shall apply to the State of Sikkim including representation in Lok Sabha, Legislative Assembly, and protection of customary laws and land rights.
simplified_text: Special provisions for Sikkim

title: Special provision with respect to the State of Mizoram
original_text: No Act of Parliament in respect of religious or social practices of the Mizos, Mizo customary law and procedure, administration of civil and criminal justice involving decisions according to Mizo customary law, and ownership and transfer of land shall apply to the State of Mizoram unless the Legislative Assembly of Mizoram by a resolution so decides.
simplified_text: Special provisions for Mizoram regarding customary law

title: Special provision with respect to the State of Arunachal Pradesh
original_text: The Legislative Assembly of the State of Arunachal Pradesh shall consist of not less than forty members. The Governor shall have special responsibility with respect to law and order in the State so long as the Legislative Assembly has less than thirty members.
simplified_text: Special provisions for Arunachal Pradesh regarding customary law

title: Special provision with respect to the State of Goa
original_text: The Legislative Assembly of the State of Goa shall consist of not less than thirty members.
simplified_text: Legislative Assembly of Goa shall have not less than thirty members

title: Special provisions with respect to the State of Karnataka
original_text: The President may provide for equitable allocation of funds for developmental expenditure over the State of Karnataka, having regard to the requirements of the different areas of the State, particularly Hyderabad-Karnataka region.
simplified_text: Equitable opportunities for people of different regions in Karnataka

title: Continuance in force of existing laws and their adaptation
original_text: All the law in force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall continue in force therein until altered or repealed or amended by a competent Legislature or other competent authority.
simplified_text: Pre-Constitution laws continue until amended or repealed

title: Power of President to make order in respect of persons under preventive detention in certain cases
original_text: Until provision is made by Parliament under clause (7) of article 22 or until the expiration of one year from the commencement of this Constitution, whichever is earlier, article 22 shall have effect as if any reference to Parliament in clauses (4) and (7) were substituted a reference to the President.
simplified_text: President can make orders regarding preventive detention

title: Provisions as to Judges of the Federal Court and proceedings pending in the Federal Court or before His Majesty in Council
original_text: The Judges of the Federal Court holding office immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall become Judges of the Supreme Court. All proceedings pending in the Federal Court at such commencement shall stand transferred to the Supreme Court.
simplified_text: Federal Court judges become Supreme Court judges

title: Provisions as to Judges of High Courts
original_text: Judges of a High Court in any Province holding office immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall become the Judges of the High Court in the corresponding State.
simplified_text: Pre-Constitution High Court judges continue

title: Provisions as to Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
original_text: The Auditor-General of India holding office immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall become the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
simplified_text: Pre-Constitution Auditor General continues

title: Provisions as to Public Service Commissions
original_text: A Public Service Commission functioning in any State immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall continue to function as the Public Service Commission for that State.
simplified_text: Pre-Constitution PSCs continue

title: Overview and objectives
original_text:
Empowers citizens to access government information and promotes transparency and accountability
Objectives:
- To provide for setting out the practical regime of right to information for citizens
- To promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority
- To empower the citizens and promote democracy
- To contain corruption and make government accountable to the governed

title: Short title, extent and commencement
original_text: This Act may be called the Right to Information Act, 2005. It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
simplified_text: Name and applicability of the Act

title: Definitions
original_text: In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires: 'appropriate Government' means in relation to a public authority which is established, constituted, owned, controlled or substantially financed by the Central Government or the Union territory administration, the Central Government; 'information' means any material in any form, including records, documents, memos, e-mails, opinions, advices, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, contracts, reports, papers, samples, models, data material held in any electronic form.
simplified_text: Key terms defined in the Act

title: Right to information
original_text: All citizens shall have the right to information subject to the provisions of this Act. All authorities shall be bound to provide information to any citizen who requests information.
simplified_text: Citizens' right to seek information

title: Obligations of public authorities
original_text: Every public authority shall: (a) maintain all its records duly catalogued and indexed; (b) publish various information including particulars of its organisation, functions and duties; (c) publish the manner of execution of subsidy programmes; (d) publish details of recipients of concessions, permits or authorisations granted.
simplified_text: Duties of government bodies

title: Designation of Public Information Officers
original_text: Every public authority shall designate as many officers as Public Information Officers (PIOs) in all administrative units or offices under it as may be necessary to provide information to persons requesting for the information.
simplified_text: Appointment of officers to handle RTI requests

title: Request for obtaining information
original_text: A person, who desires to obtain any information under this Act, shall make a request in writing or through electronic means in English or Hindi or in the official language of the area, to the Public Information Officer, specifying the particulars of the information sought by him.
simplified_text: Procedure for requesting information

title: Disposal of request
original_text: The Public Information Officer shall provide the information within thirty days from the date of receipt of the request. If the information concerns the life or liberty of a person, it shall be provided within forty-eight hours.
simplified_text: Timeline for providing information

title: Exemption from disclosure of information
original_text: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, there shall be no obligation to give any citizen: (a) information which prejudicially affects the sovereignty and integrity of India; (b) information expressly forbidden by any court; (c) information which would cause breach of privilege of Parliament or State Legislature; (d) commercial confidence, trade secrets or intellectual property.
simplified_text: Information that cannot be disclosed

title: Power to make rules
original_text: The appropriate Government may make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act including fees for obtaining information, periods within which information is to be furnished, and the form and manner of making a request.
simplified_text: Government's rule-making authority

title: Constitution of Central Information Commission
original_text: The Central Government shall constitute a body to be known as the Central Information Commission to exercise the powers conferred on, and to perform the functions assigned to, it under this Act.
simplified_text: Establishment of appellate body

title: Overview and objectives
original_text:
Protects consumer rights, provides remedies for unfair trade practices, and establishes consumer dispute redressal mechanism
Objectives:
- To protect the rights of consumers
- To establish authorities for timely and effective administration and settlement of consumers' disputes
- To provide better protection of the interests of consumers
- To prevent unfair trade practices and false advertisements

title: Definitions
original_text: 'Consumer' means any person who buys any goods for a consideration and includes any user of such goods; 'Defect' means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard; 'Service' means service of any description which is made available to potential users.
simplified_text: Key terms including consumer, defect, and service

title: Consumer Rights
original_text: Consumer rights include: (a) the right to be protected against marketing of goods and services which are hazardous to life and property; (b) the right to be informed about the quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price of goods or services; (c) the right to be assured access to a variety of goods and services at competitive prices; (d) the right to be heard; (e) the right to seek redressal; (f) the right to consumer education.
simplified_text: Six fundamental consumer rights

title: Prohibition against unfair trade practice
original_text: No person shall engage in unfair trade practice. Unfair trade practice means a trade practice which, for the purpose of promoting the sale, use or supply of any goods or services, adopts any unfair method or deceptive practice.
simplified_text: Bans misleading and deceptive practices

title: Misleading advertisement
original_text: No person shall make or publish or cause to be published any advertisement which is false or misleading or one which deliberately conceals important information.
simplified_text: Prohibition of false or misleading advertisements

title: Product liability
original_text: A product manufacturer, service provider or product seller shall be liable to compensate for harm caused to any consumer by such defective product manufactured or sold or by deficiency in services.
simplified_text: Manufacturer's liability for defective products

title: Jurisdiction of District Commission
original_text: The District Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services and compensation claimed does not exceed rupees one crore.
simplified_text: Consumer cases at district level

title: Jurisdiction of State Commission
original_text: The State Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services and compensation claimed exceeds rupees one crore but does not exceed rupees ten crores.
simplified_text: Consumer cases at state level

title: Jurisdiction of National Commission
original_text: The National Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services and compensation claimed exceeds rupees ten crores.
simplified_text: Consumer cases at national level

title: Penalty for false or misleading advertisement
original_text: Whoever manufactures or causes to be manufactured, or endorses a false or misleading advertisement shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees.
simplified_text: Punishment for false advertising

title: Penalty for non-compliance of the order of Commission
original_text: Whoever fails to comply with any order made by the District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one month but which may extend to three years, or with fine which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees but which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both.
simplified_text: Consequences of not following Commission's orders

title: Overview and objectives
original_text:
Regulates road transport, traffic rules, vehicle registration, licensing, and road safety
Objectives:
- To consolidate and amend the law relating to motor vehicles
- To provide for road safety and traffic management
- To regulate vehicle registration and licensing
- To establish penalties for traffic violations

title: Necessity for driving licence
original_text: No person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place unless he holds an effective driving licence issued to him authorising him to drive the vehicle.
simplified_text: Requirement of valid driving licence

title: Age limit for driving motor vehicles
original_text: No person under the age of eighteen years shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place. No person under the age of twenty years shall drive a transport vehicle in any public place.
simplified_text: Minimum age requirements for different vehicle types

title: Necessity for registration
original_text: No person shall drive any motor vehicle and no owner of a motor vehicle shall cause or permit the vehicle to be driven in any public place unless the vehicle is registered.
simplified_text: Vehicle registration requirements

title: Wearing of protective headgear
original_text: Every person driving or riding on a motorcycle shall, while in a public place, wear protective headgear conforming to such standards as may be prescribed.
simplified_text: Helmet mandatory for two-wheeler riders

title: Duty to wear seat-belt
original_text: The driver and person seated in the front seat of a motor vehicle shall wear seat-belts while the vehicle is in motion.
simplified_text: Seat belt mandatory for car occupants

title: Duty to obey traffic signs
original_text: The driver of a motor vehicle in a public place shall observe and comply with all traffic signs displayed.
simplified_text: Compliance with traffic signals and signs

title: Limits of speed
original_text: No person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place at a speed exceeding the maximum speed or at a speed less than the minimum speed fixed for the vehicle under this Act.
simplified_text: Speed restrictions for different vehicles

title: Dangerous driving
original_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle at a speed or in a manner which is dangerous to the public, having regard to all the circumstances, shall be punishable for the first offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
simplified_text: Prohibition of rash and negligent driving

title: Necessity for insurance against third party risk
original_text: No person shall use, except as a passenger, or cause or allow any other person to use, a motor vehicle in a public place, unless there is in force in relation to the use of the vehicle by that person a policy of insurance complying with the requirements of this Chapter.
simplified_text: Mandatory vehicle insurance

title: Offences relating to licences
original_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle in contravention of section 3 shall be punishable for the first offence with a fine of five thousand rupees, and for any second or subsequent offence with a fine of ten thousand rupees.
simplified_text: Penalties for driving without licence

title: Driving vehicles in contravention of section 56
original_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle or causes or allows a motor vehicle to be used in contravention of the provisions of section 39 shall be punishable with a fine of ten thousand rupees.
simplified_text: Penalties for unregistered vehicles

title: Driving at excessive speed
original_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle in excess of the speed limit shall be liable to pay a penalty which may extend to one thousand rupees for light motor vehicles and two thousand rupees for medium or heavy motor vehicles.
simplified_text: Penalties for overspeeding

title: Driving dangerously
original_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle at a speed or in a manner which is dangerous to the public shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both for first offence; and with imprisonment which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees or with both for second or subsequent offence.
simplified_text: Enhanced penalties for dangerous driving

title: Driving by a drunken person or by a person under the influence of drugs
original_text: Whoever drives or attempts to drive a motor vehicle having consumed alcohol exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml of blood shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both.
simplified_text: Prohibition and penalties for drunk driving

title: Driving without insurance
original_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle without a valid insurance policy shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with fine of two thousand rupees, or with both.
simplified_text: Penalties for driving uninsured vehicle

title: Penalties and fines
original_text:
- Driving without licence (Section 3, 177): ₹5,000 (first offence), ₹10,000 (subsequent offences); imprisonment: Not applicable
- Driving without registration (Section 39, 181): ₹10,000; imprisonment: Not applicable
- Driving without insurance (Section 146, 194): ₹2,000; imprisonment: Up to 3 months or both
- Overspeeding (Section 183): ₹1,000 (light vehicles), ₹2,000 (medium/heavy vehicles); imprisonment: Not applicable
- Dangerous/Rash driving (Section 184): ₹1,000 to ₹5,000; imprisonment: Up to 6 months (first), up to 2 years (subsequent)
- Drunk driving (Section 185): ₹10,000; imprisonment: Up to 6 months or both
- Not wearing helmet (two-wheeler) (Section 129, 177): ₹1,000 + Disqualification of licence for 3 months; imprisonment: Not applicable
- Not wearing seat belt (Section 130, 177): ₹1,000; imprisonment: Not applicable
- Jumping red light/Disobeying traffic signals (Section 132, 177): ₹1,000 to ₹5,000; imprisonment: Not applicable
- Using mobile phone while driving (Section 177): ₹1,000 (first), ₹10,000 (subsequent); imprisonment: Not applicable
- Overloading (goods vehicle) (Section 194): ₹20,000 + ₹2,000 per extra tonne; imprisonment: Not applicable
- Overloading (passenger vehicle) (Section 194A): ₹1,000 per extra passenger; imprisonment: Not applicable
- Racing and driving at high speed (Section 189): ₹5,000; imprisonment: Up to 1 month or both
- Driving under-age (Section 5, 181): ₹5,000 + Guardian liable for ₹25,000; imprisonment: Up to 3 years for guardian
- Driving without permit (commercial) (Section 192A): ₹10,000 (first), ₹10,000 + vehicle seizure (subsequent); imprisonment: Not applicable
- Violation of road regulations (Section 177): ₹500 (general traffic violations); imprisonment: Not applicable
- Causing obstruction to free flow of traffic (Section 122): ₹500 to ₹1,000; imprisonment: Not applicable
- Not giving way to emergency vehicles (Section 194E): ₹10,000; imprisonment: Not applicable
- Driving with defective brakes/lights (Section 190): ₹500 to ₹1,500; imprisonment: Not applicable
- Carrying goods on roof (Section 177): ₹1,000; imprisonment: Not applicable

title: Overview and objectives
original_text:
Defines crimes and prescribes punishments for various offences in India
Objectives:
- To provide a general penal code for India
- To define various criminal offences
- To prescribe punishments for crimes
- To ensure uniformity in criminal law across India

title: Common intention
original_text: When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each of such persons is liable for that act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone.
simplified_text: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention

title: Punishments
original_text: The punishments to which offenders are liable under the provisions of this Code are: Death, Imprisonment for life, Imprisonment (rigorous or simple), Forfeiture of property, and Fine.
simplified_text: Types of punishments under IPC

title: Act done by a person bound by law
original_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who is bound by law to do it.
simplified_text: No crime if act done under legal obligation

title: Act done by a person justified by law
original_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by any person who is justified by law in doing it.
simplified_text: Justifiable acts not crimes

title: Accident in doing a lawful act
original_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by accident or misfortune, and without any criminal intention or knowledge in the doing of a lawful act in a lawful manner by lawful means and with proper care and caution.
simplified_text: No crime if act done accidentally

title: Right of private defence
original_text: Nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence.
simplified_text: Right to defend oneself and property

title: Right of private defence of body extending to causing death
original_text: The right of private defence of the body extends to the voluntary causing of death if the offence occasions reasonable apprehension of death, grievous hurt, rape, or kidnapping.
simplified_text: When self-defence can extend to causing death

title: Waging war against Government of India
original_text: Whoever wages war against the Government of India, or attempts to wage such war, or abets the waging of such war, shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified_text: Punishment for waging war against the nation

title: Sedition
original_text: Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or otherwise, brings or attempts to bring into hatred or contempt, or excites or attempts to excite disaffection towards the Government established by law shall be punished with imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added, or with imprisonment which may extend to three years, to which fine may be added, or with fine.
simplified_text: Bringing hatred or contempt towards Government (under review)

title: Culpable homicide
original_text: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide.
simplified_text: Definition of culpable homicide

title: Murder
original_text: Culpable homicide is murder if the act by which the death is caused is done with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as the offender knows to be likely to cause the death of the person to whom the harm is caused.
simplified_text: Definition of murder

title: Punishment for murder
original_text: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified_text: Death penalty or life imprisonment for murder

title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
original_text: Whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified_text: Lesser punishment for culpable homicide

title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
original_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified_text: Punishment for outraging modesty of women

title: Rape
original_text: A man is said to commit rape if he has sexual intercourse with a woman under circumstances falling under any of the seven descriptions enumerated in this section, including without her consent, with her consent obtained under fear of death or hurt, or when she is unable to understand the nature of the act.
simplified_text: Definition of rape

title: Punishment for rape
original_text: Whoever commits rape shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified_text: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years for rape

title: Theft
original_text: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
simplified_text: Definition of theft

title: Punishment for theft
original_text: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
simplified_text: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both for theft

title: Punishment for dacoity
original_text: Whoever commits dacoity shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified_text: Life imprisonment or rigorous imprisonment for dacoity

title: Cheating
original_text: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to 'cheat'.
simplified_text: Definition of cheating

title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
original_text: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified_text: Punishment for cheating - imprisonment up to 7 years

title: Defamation
original_text: Whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm, the reputation of such person, is said to defame that person.
simplified_text: Making or publishing false imputations harming reputation

title: Punishment for defamation
original_text: Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
simplified_text: Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both

title: Criminal intimidation
original_text: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do, commits criminal intimidation.
simplified_text: Threatening to cause injury to person, reputation or property

title: Punishment for attempting to commit offences
original_text: Whoever attempts to commit an offence punishable by this Code with imprisonment for life or imprisonment, or to cause such an offence to be committed, and in such attempt does any act towards the commission of the offence, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one-half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for that offence.
simplified_text: Attempt to commit offence punishable

title: Overview and objectives
original_text:
Governs civil court procedures, jurisdiction, and execution of decrees
Objectives:
- To consolidate and amend the laws relating to the procedure of Courts of Civil Judicature
- To ensure speedy disposal of civil cases
- To provide for jurisdiction of civil courts
- To regulate execution of civil decrees and orders

title: Courts to try all civil suits unless barred
original_text: The Courts shall have jurisdiction to try all suits of a civil nature excepting suits of which their cognizance is either expressly or impliedly barred.
simplified_text: Jurisdiction of civil courts

title: Stay of suit
original_text: No Court shall proceed with the trial of any suit in which the matter in issue is also directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit.
simplified_text: Court may stay suit if matter is pending elsewhere

title: Institution of suits
original_text: Every suit shall be instituted by the presentation of a plaint to the Court or to such officer as it appoints in this behalf.
simplified_text: How to file a civil suit

title: Notice to Government
original_text: No suit shall be instituted against the Government until the expiration of two months next after notice in writing has been delivered to the appropriate authority.
simplified_text: Two months' notice required before suing government

title: Examination of witnesses
original_text: The Court may examine such witnesses as it thinks fit, and the parties or their pleaders shall be entitled to cross-examine them.
simplified_text: Court's power to examine witnesses

title: Second appeal
original_text: Save as otherwise expressly provided in the body of this Code or by any other law for the time being in force, an appeal shall lie to the High Court from every decree passed in appeal by any Court subordinate to the High Court, if the High Court is satisfied that the case involves a substantial question of law.
simplified_text: Appeal on substantial question of law

title: Revision
original_text: The High Court may call for the record of any case which has been decided by any Court subordinate to such High Court and in which no appeal lies thereto, and if such subordinate Court appears to have exercised a jurisdiction not vested in it by law, or to have failed to exercise a jurisdiction so vested, or to have acted in the exercise of its jurisdiction illegally or with material irregularity, the High Court may make such order in the case as it thinks fit.
simplified_text: High Court's revisional jurisdiction

title: Inherent powers of Court
original_text: Nothing in this Code shall be deemed to limit or otherwise affect the inherent power of the Court to make such orders as may be necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the Court.
simplified_text: Court's power to make orders to prevent abuse of process

act_or_case_name: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
act_aliases: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
title: Overview and objectives
original_text:
Provides free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14 years
Objectives:
- To provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years
- To ensure quality elementary education
- To promote social justice and equality in education
- To make education a fundamental right

act_or_case_name: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
act_aliases: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
title: Right of child to free and compulsory education
original_text: Every child of the age of six to fourteen years shall have a right to free and compulsory elementary education in a neighbourhood school till completion of elementary education.
simplified_text: Every child has right to elementary education

act_or_case_name: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
act_aliases: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
title: Extent of school to be specified
original_text: For the purposes of this Act, a school means any recognised school imparting elementary education and includes a school established, owned, controlled or substantially financed by the appropriate Government or local authority.
simplified_text: Types of schools covered under RTE

act_or_case_name: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
act_aliases: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
title: No capitation fee and screening procedure for admission
original_text: No school or person shall, while admitting a child, collect any capitation fee and subject the child or his or her parents or guardians to any screening procedure.
simplified_text: Prohibition of capitation fees and entrance tests

act_or_case_name: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
act_aliases: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
title: Proof of age for admission
original_text: For the purpose of admission to elementary education, the age of a child shall be determined on the basis of the birth certificate or on the basis of such other document as may be prescribed.
simplified_text: Age determination for school admission

act_or_case_name: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
act_aliases: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
title: Pupil-teacher ratio
original_text: The pupil-teacher ratio shall be thirty students per teacher for primary classes and thirty-five students per teacher for upper primary classes.
simplified_text: Maximum students per teacher

act_or_case_name: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
act_aliases: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
title: Minimum qualifications for teachers
original_text: Any person possessing such minimum qualifications as laid down by the National Council for Teacher Education shall be eligible for appointment as a teacher.
simplified_text: Required qualifications for teaching

act_or_case_name: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
act_aliases: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
title: Prohibition of deployment of teachers for non-educational purposes
original_text: No teacher shall be deployed for any non-educational purposes other than decennial population census, disaster relief duties or duties relating to elections to the local authority or the State Legislatures or Parliament.
simplified_text: Teachers cannot be used for non-teaching work

act_or_case_name: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
act_aliases: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
title: Curriculum and evaluation procedure
original_text: The curriculum and the evaluation procedure shall be laid down by the appropriate Government on the recommendation of the National Council of Educational Research and Training and the State Council of Educational Research and Training, which shall conform to the values enshrined in the Constitution and which shall be based on the principle of learning through activities, discovery and exploration in a child friendly and child centered manner.
simplified_text: Child-friendly curriculum required

act_or_case_name: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
act_aliases: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
title: Examination and completion certificate
original_text: No child admitted in a school shall be required to pass any Board examination till completion of elementary education. Every child completing elementary education shall be awarded a certificate in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed.
simplified_text: No detention policy and completion certificate

title: Overview and objectives
original_text:
Provides legal framework for electronic governance and addresses cybercrimes
Objectives:
- To provide legal recognition for transactions carried out by electronic means
- To facilitate electronic filing of documents with Government agencies
- To prevent computer-based crimes
- To establish legal framework for e-governance and e-commerce

title: Penalty for damage to computer systems
original_text: If any person without permission of the owner destroys, deletes or alters any information residing in a computer resource or diminishes its value or utility or affects it injuriously, he shall be liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the person so affected.
simplified_text: Compensation for unauthorized access or damage

title: Tampering with computer source documents
original_text: Whoever knowingly or intentionally conceals, destroys or alters or causes another to conceal, destroy or alter any computer source code used for a computer program with the intention of causing damage, shall be punishable with imprisonment up to three years, or with fine which may extend to two lakh rupees, or with both.
simplified_text: Punishment for altering source code

title: Computer related offences
original_text: If any person, dishonestly or fraudulently, does any act referred to in section 43, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees or with both.
simplified_text: Hacking and unauthorized access punishable

title: Punishment for sending offensive messages (Struck Down)
original_text: Section 66A which punished sending offensive messages through communication service was declared unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015) as it violated freedom of speech and expression.
simplified_text: This section was struck down by Supreme Court in 2015

title: Punishment for dishonestly receiving stolen computer resource
original_text: Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen computer resource or communication device knowing or having reason to believe the same to be stolen computer resource or communication device, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to rupees one lakh or with both.
simplified_text: Receiving stolen digital property

title: Punishment for identity theft
original_text: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly makes use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to rupees one lakh.
simplified_text: Using another person's digital identity

title: Punishment for cheating by personation using computer resource
original_text: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.
simplified_text: Online impersonation and fraud

title: Punishment for violation of privacy
original_text: Whoever, intentionally or knowingly captures, publishes or transmits the image of a private area of any person without his or her consent, under circumstances violating the privacy of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years or with fine not exceeding two lakh rupees, or with both.
simplified_text: Capturing or transmitting private images without consent

title: Punishment for publishing obscene information
original_text: Whoever publishes or transmits or causes to be published or transmitted in the electronic form, any material which is lascivious or appeals to the prurient interest or tends to deprave and corrupt persons, shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees.
simplified_text: Publishing obscene content electronically

title: Punishment for publishing sexually explicit material
original_text: Whoever publishes or transmits material containing sexually explicit act in electronic form shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees.
simplified_text: Stronger punishment for sexually explicit content

title: Punishment for child pornography
original_text: Whoever publishes or transmits material depicting children in sexually explicit act in electronic form shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees and in the event of second or subsequent conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and also with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees.
simplified_text: Severe punishment for child sexual abuse material

title: Power to issue directions for interception or monitoring
original_text: The Central Government or a State Government or any officer specially authorised may, if satisfied that it is necessary or expedient to do so in the interest of the sovereignty or integrity of India, issue directions for interception or monitoring of any information through any computer resource.
simplified_text: Government's power to monitor electronic information

act_or_case_name: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
act_aliases: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Overview and objectives
original_text:
Prevents and addresses sexual harassment of women at workplace
Objectives:
- To provide protection against sexual harassment of women at workplace
- To prevent and prohibit sexual harassment
- To provide for redressal of complaints
- To ensure safe working environment for women

act_or_case_name: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
act_aliases: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Definitions - Sexual Harassment
original_text: Sexual harassment includes unwelcome sexually determined behaviour such as: (a) physical contact and advances; (b) demand or request for sexual favours; (c) making sexually coloured remarks; (d) showing pornography; (e) any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature.
simplified_text: What constitutes sexual harassment

act_or_case_name: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
act_aliases: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Prevention of sexual harassment
original_text: No woman shall be subjected to sexual harassment at any workplace.
simplified_text: Prohibition of sexual harassment

act_or_case_name: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
act_aliases: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Constitution of Internal Complaints Committee
original_text: Every employer of a workplace shall constitute an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) at each office or branch with 10 or more employees. The ICC shall consist of: (a) a Presiding Officer who is a woman employed at a senior level; (b) not less than two Members from amongst employees committed to the cause of women; (c) one external Member from amongst NGOs or associations committed to women's cause.
simplified_text: Mandatory committee in every workplace

act_or_case_name: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
act_aliases: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Complaint of sexual harassment
original_text: Any aggrieved woman may make a complaint of sexual harassment at workplace in writing to the Internal Committee within a period of three months from the date of incident. The ICC may extend the time limit by another three months for reasons to be recorded in writing.
simplified_text: How to file a complaint

act_or_case_name: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
act_aliases: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Inquiry into complaint
original_text: The Internal Committee shall complete the inquiry within a period of ninety days from the date of receipt of the complaint.
simplified_text: Investigation process

act_or_case_name: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
act_aliases: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Duties of employer
original_text: Every employer shall: (a) provide a safe working environment; (b) display the penal consequences of sexual harassment; (c) organize workshops and awareness programmes; (d) assist in securing the attendance of respondent and witnesses; (e) make available necessary facilities to the Internal Committee; (f) assist the woman if she chooses to file a complaint in relation to the offence under the Indian Penal Code.
simplified_text: Employer's responsibilities

act_or_case_name: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
act_aliases: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Penalty for non-compliance
original_text: Any employer who fails to constitute an Internal Committee or comply with any provisions of this Act shall be punishable with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees.
simplified_text: Punishment for not complying with the Act

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
act_aliases: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Overview and objectives
original_text:
Protects children from sexual abuse, harassment, and pornography
Objectives:
- To protect children from offences of sexual assault, sexual harassment and pornography
- To establish Special Courts for trial of such offences
- To provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
- To safeguard the interests and well-being of the child

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
act_aliases: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Definitions - Child
original_text: A 'child' means any person below the age of eighteen years.
simplified_text: Any person below 18 years

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
act_aliases: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Penetrative sexual assault
original_text: A person is said to commit penetrative sexual assault if he penetrates his penis or any object into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a child.
simplified_text: Definition of serious sexual assault on child

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
act_aliases: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Punishment for penetrative sexual assault
original_text: Whoever commits penetrative sexual assault shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified_text: Minimum 10 years imprisonment

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
act_aliases: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Aggravated penetrative sexual assault
original_text: Aggravated penetrative sexual assault includes assault by police officer, armed forces, public servant, relative, or assault causing grievous hurt or mental illness to the child.
simplified_text: More serious forms of assault

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
act_aliases: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault
original_text: Whoever commits aggravated penetrative sexual assault shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall be liable to fine. In case death occurs, punishment shall be life imprisonment or death penalty.
simplified_text: Minimum 20 years to life imprisonment

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
act_aliases: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Sexual harassment of the child
original_text: A person is said to commit sexual harassment upon a child when such person with sexual intent: (a) utters any word or makes any sound, or makes any gesture with the intention that such word or sound shall be heard, or such gesture shall be seen by the child; (b) exhibits any object to a child with the intention that such object shall be seen by the child; (c) shows any object in any form or media for pornographic purposes to the child.
simplified_text: Definition of sexual harassment

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
act_aliases: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Use of child for pornographic purposes
original_text: Whoever uses a child for pornographic purposes shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to five years and with fine.
simplified_text: Child pornography offence

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
act_aliases: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Storage of pornographic material involving child
original_text: Any person who stores for commercial purposes any pornographic material in any form involving a child shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years or with fine or with both.
simplified_text: Possession of child sexual abuse material

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
act_aliases: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Reporting of sexual offences
original_text: Any person who has apprehension that an offence under this Act is likely to be committed or has knowledge that such an offence has been committed, shall provide such information to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or the local police.
simplified_text: Mandatory reporting requirement

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
act_aliases: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Procedure for recording statement of child
original_text: The statement of the child shall be recorded at the residence of the child or at the place of his choice in the presence of the parents or any other person in whom the child has trust or confidence.
simplified_text: Child-friendly recording of statement

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
act_aliases: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Protection of identity
original_text: No person shall make any report or present any comments in any media or publish any contents which discloses the identity of the child including his name, address, school, or any other particular which may lead to disclosure of identity of the child.
simplified_text: Media cannot disclose child's identity

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
act_aliases: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Overview and objectives
original_text:
Protects women from domestic violence and provides relief and rehabilitation
Objectives:
- To provide for more effective protection of the rights of women guaranteed under the Constitution who are victims of violence of any kind occurring within the family
- To provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
- To ensure right to reside in the shared household
- To provide immediate relief and support to victims

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
act_aliases: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Definitions - Aggrieved person
original_text: 'Aggrieved person' means any woman who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondent and who alleges to have been subjected to any act of domestic violence by the respondent.
simplified_text: Who can file complaint

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
act_aliases: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Definition of domestic violence
original_text: Any act, omission or commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute domestic violence in case it: (a) harms or injures or endangers the health, safety, life, limb or well-being, whether mental or physical, of the aggrieved person; (b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved person with a view to coerce her to meet any unlawful demand for any dowry; (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved person; (d) otherwise injures or causes harm, whether physical or mental, to the aggrieved person.
simplified_text: What constitutes domestic violence

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
act_aliases: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Application to Magistrate
original_text: An aggrieved person or a Protection Officer or any other person on behalf of the aggrieved person may present an application to the Magistrate seeking one or more reliefs under this Act.
simplified_text: How to seek protection

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
act_aliases: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Right to reside in a shared household
original_text: Every woman in a domestic relationship shall have the right to reside in the shared household, whether or not she has any right, title or beneficial interest in the same. The aggrieved person shall not be evicted or excluded from the shared household except in accordance with the procedure established by law.
simplified_text: Woman's right to continue living in matrimonial home

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
act_aliases: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Protection orders
original_text: The Magistrate may pass a protection order prohibiting the respondent from: (a) committing any act of domestic violence; (b) aiding or abetting in the commission of acts of domestic violence; (c) entering the place of employment of the aggrieved person; (d) attempting to communicate with the aggrieved person; (e) alienating any assets used by both parties; (f) causing violence to dependents or relatives of the aggrieved person.
simplified_text: Court can prohibit respondent from committing violence

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
act_aliases: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Residence orders
original_text: The Magistrate may pass a residence order: (a) restraining the respondent from dispossessing the aggrieved person from the shared household; (b) directing the respondent to remove himself from the shared household; (c) restraining the respondent from entering the shared household; (d) directing the respondent to secure same level of alternate accommodation for the aggrieved person.
simplified_text: Orders regarding shared household

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
act_aliases: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Monetary reliefs
original_text: The Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person including: (a) loss of earnings; (b) medical expenses; (c) loss caused due to the destruction of property; (d) maintenance for the aggrieved person and her children; (e) custody of the child.
simplified_text: Financial support to victim

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
act_aliases: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Custody orders
original_text: The Magistrate may grant temporary custody of any child to the aggrieved person or the person making an application on her behalf and specify the arrangements for visit of such child by the respondent.

act_or_case_name: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

title: Penalty for breach of protection order by respondent
original_text: A breach of protection order, or of an interim protection order, by the respondent shall be an offence and shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees, or with both.
